title: An MCP server for Dynamics 365 Business Central? Why not?
summary: Explains the Model Context Protocol, an open standard from Anthropic for connecting AI apps to tools and data, and contrasts it with function calling. The author argues MCP suits Business Central and demos an alpha Admin Center MCP server that lists installed AppSource apps, checks for updates and schedules them from GitHub Copilot agent mode or Cursor.
key_points: MCP gives AI apps one standard way to reach external tools and data instead of a custom integration per source
Function calling produces provider-specific structured calls; MCP standardizes tool discovery, invocation and response handling
MCP uses a client-server model built from hosts, clients, servers and data sources
The author's alpha Business Central Admin Center MCP server exposes tools to list AppSource apps, find updates and schedule an update
The same server works from any MCP-capable tool such as GitHub Copilot or Cursor; the protocol is still new and evolving
